text: If some point is taken inside a circle, and more than two equal straight-lines radiate from the point towards the (circumference of the) circle, (then) the point taken is the center of the circle. Let $ABC$ be a circle, and $D$ a point inside it, and let more than two equal straight-lines, $DA$, $DB$, and $DC$, radiate from $D$ towards (the circumference of) circle $ABC$. I say that point $D$ is the center of circle $ABC$.
For let $AB$ and $BC$ be joined, and (then) be cut in half at points $E$ and $F$ (respectively) [Prop.~1.10].
And $ED$ and $FD$ being joined, let them be drawn through to points $G$, $K$, $H$, and $L$.
Therefore, since $AE$ is equal to $EB$, and $ED$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AE$, $ED$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BE$, $ED$ (respectively).
assertion: AE, ED equal BE, ED respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $AE$, $ED$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BE$, $ED$ (respectively)

text: And the base $DA$ (is) equal to the base $DB$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the base $DA$ (is) equal to the base $DB$

text: Thus, angle $AED$ is equal to angle $BED$ [Prop.~1.8].

assertion: angles AED and BED are each right-angles

text: And since, if some straight-line in a circle cuts some (other) straight-line in half, and at right-angles, (then) the center of the circle is on the former (straight-line) [Prop.~3.1~corr.], the center of the circle is thus on $GK$.
assertion: center of circle is on GK

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: if some straight-line in a circle cuts some (other) straight-line in half, and at right-angles, (then) the center of the circle is on the former (straight-line)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the center of the circle is thus on $GK$

text: So, for the same (reasons), the center of circle $ABC$ is also on $HL$.
assertion: center of circle ABC is also on HL

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the center of circle $ABC$ is also on $HL$

text: And the straight-lines $GK$ and $HL$ have no common (point) other than point $D$.
assertion: GK and HL have no common point other than D

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the straight-lines $GK$ and $HL$ have no common (point) other than point $D$

text: Thus, point $D$ is the center of circle $ABC$.
assertion: point D is the center of circle ABC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: point $D$ is the center of circle $ABC$

text: Thus, if some point is taken inside a circle, and more than two equal straight-lines radiate from the point towards the (circumference of the) circle, (then) the point taken is the center of the circle. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
